sentences.text: The fact that the accident occurred and the further fact that the offending vehicle was insured is not in dispute.

3. The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence, has recorded a finding that the claimant has suffered the following injuries:
a) fracture of tibia left and fracture of fibula left.
b) Left knee and ankle movements are restricted and painful.
4. The insurer contends that the percentage of disability assessed by the Tribunal is incorrect and the compensation awarded in respect of several heads are on higher side.
Whereas the claimant contends that the notional income determined by the Tribunal is on lower side and the sums awarded towards pain and suffering, loss of amenities etc. are also on lower side.
5. The doctor, who was examined has stated that the claimant had suffered 30% disability to particular limb.
The Tribunal has determined the disability at 25% to the whole body, which would be incorrect.
It would therefore be appropriate to assessed the permanent disability at 10%.
6. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.7,500/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
which, for the accident of the year, 2015 would be Rs.9,000/-.
7. As the claimant was aged 44 years, a multiplier of '14' would have to be applied.
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,51,200/- (Rs.9,000 x 12 x 14 x 10%) towards 'loss of future income' .
8. As a consequence, the amount of Rs.25,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards 'loss of income during the laid up period' would also stand enhanced to Rs.27,000/- (9,000 X 3 months).
9. Having regard to the injuries suffered by the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' as against Rs.40,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

10. Having regard to the lasting effects of the injuries on the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities, as against the sum of Rs.25,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
